scope: Consolidation of already inspected primary sources and existing local files. No live block-device ioctl, kernel module loading, driver change, new VM run, or host configuration change.

source_facts.target: multipath block device file descriptor, not /dev/mapper/control
semantics: Probes currently Active paths only in current path group, sequentially, reading sector 0 for one logical block on each selected underlying block device.
Marks a path failed only for statuses satisfying blk_path_error; does not compare returned contents or validate PV/VG/layout identity.
Uses submit_bio_wait and can block behind stalled underlying I/O; no independent hard completion deadline is provided by this routine.
Does not reinstate already failed paths. Does not automatically start a periodic monitoring task.

Returns -ENOTCONN when no valid paths remain globally; returns 0 if valid paths remain, including possible unprobed paths in other groups. Allocation errors may return -ENOMEM; oversized logical block check may return -EINVAL.
In v7.0 source the probe can skip I/O during some initialization/presuspend states. Thus return 0 is not a complete storage-health certificate.
Concurrent probes may wait for one probe and skip repeated probing if the current group is unchanged; group-switch messages may defer their effect until probing completes.

local_module_binary_inspection.method: Decompress existing .ko.zst in memory and search exact printable strings for symbol names; this is supporting binary evidence, not a runtime ioctl test or full ELF/disassembly proof.

public_summary: Linux 7.0 includes an on-demand DM multipath active-path probe interface introduced in Linux 6.16.
The installed Ubuntu 7.0 kernel header defines it; the saved Ubuntu 7.0 multipath module contains probe-related symbol strings absent from the saved Ubuntu 6.8-139 module.
The fixed multipath-tools 0.15.0 source has no detected call to this interface; upgrading userspace to 0.15 alone is not evidence of using it.
It is a candidate backend for an optional, limited-frequency path probe, not a replacement for medium identity admission, transaction takeover, progress observation, or durability validation.
No runtime correctness, latency, CPU, or memory benefit of this interface has been measured in this project.
limitations: The semantic reading uses upstream v7.0 source; local Ubuntu header/module inspection supports presence but is not a full Ubuntu source-patch audit.
Absence of a source token or binary string is bounded static evidence; it is not a direct runtime unsupported-ioctl observation on the old kernel.
A positive probe result covers neither all path groups nor data integrity or application survival.

private_evidence.includes: Complete per-file source hash inventory and original inspected paths.
